Budget exhausted. Despite extensive probing (block/statement compilation edge cases, builtin-shadowing gates, mutual tail-recursion cost accounting, deep_eq/binop hot paths, builtin argument-order/type edge cases, num() parsing, and self_eval differential runs), I was unable to find a program on which any oracle actually fires. The one genuine oddity I found — `join`'s error message reporting the offending *value* instead of its *index* (e.g. `join([1,"ok","ok3",5], ",")` says `"element 5 is not a string"` when 5 is the value at index 3, not an index) — never triggers any oracle: it doesn't crash (totality), both fast/slow/direct paths call the same `b_join` so they agree, determinism is unaffected, and self_eval explicitly exempts miss-wording differences. Per the instructions, I'm not reporting it since I have no firing reproducer.
